Definition: from G3844 and G1521; to lead in aside, i.e. introduce surreptitiously:--privily bring in.
BiblicalUsage: Pareisago means to bring in privily, to lead in on the side. It appears once, in 2 Peter 2:1, where false prophets among the people are matched by false teachers among believers, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe false teaching never knocks on the front door, it slips in the side, and the church must watch its side doors as well as its front.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
